---
title: "Beyond Rankings: Benchmark-Informed Method Recommendation"
---

**Speaker:** [Jean Yang](https://profiles.sydney.edu.au/jean.yang), University of Sydney

### Abstract {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Computational biology increasingly relies on benchmarks to compare methods across datasets, tasks and evaluation metrics, yet benchmark evidence is most often consumed as static rankings. This limits the reuse of the information embedded in benchmark studies, especially in settings where methods exhibit context-specific strengths rather than a single overall optimum. Motivated by benchmarking problems in settings such as gene-expression-guided molecule generation, where models may pass basic validity checks but later fail chemical, structural, or biological triage, we introduce Benchmark-Informed Representation Learning (BIRL). BIRL treats benchmark outcomes as structured scientific resources that link datasets, methods, and evaluation endpoints, from which reusable representations of analytical behaviour can be learned. We evaluate whether these representations can transfer benchmark-derived information to unseen datasets and inform dataset-aware method recommendation. Across benchmark studies spanning different biological data modalities and analytical tasks, BIRL identifies reproducible benchmark structures and preserves some method-ranking relationships in held-out settings. Although performance varies across studies, our overall results suggest that benchmark outcomes contain reusable information about dataset-specific computational behaviour.
